key_insight: Surrogate-assisted Bayesian calibration predicts stator differential-mode impedance accurately, but requires effective material parameters that deviate from datasheets, signaling incomplete material models.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports early EV electromagnetic compatibility assessment by estimating unknown stator material properties from impedance measurements.
method: Replace costly 3D full-wave finite element simulations with a multi-output surrogate.
Calibrate effective material parameters using Hamiltonian Markov chain Monte Carlo.
Assess model completeness with an orthogonal, surrogate-compliant discrepancy term.
evidence_signal: Against broadband differential-mode impedance measurements up to 30 MHz, two of three parameter-range scenarios achieved good agreement; datasheet-aligned calibration was deficient.
watch_item: Calibration covers stator differential-mode impedance only; rotor effects and common-mode impedance remain unvalidated.
paper_title: Bayesian Calibration of Effective Material Parameters in Electric Machine Stators
